part_title: Amazon Kendra Enterprise Search and Retrieval Quality

scenes.title: Amazon Kendra: From Documents to Answers
scenes.narration: The slide begins with enterprise knowledge sources: PDFs and text in S3 plus supported systems such as SharePoint, Google Drive and Confluence. Kendra connectors synchronise content into a search index, and a person submits a natural-language question about vacation or parental-leave policies. Kendra ranks relevant passages and returns answers or excerpts with source links. The lower panels emphasise two boundaries. First, this is search and ranking, not a large language model inventing a new response. Second, document permissions and user identity context must be preserved where supported so the search does not leak documents from another team. The newest content available to queries depends on successful synchronisation, so the index may lag behind the original repository. In a GenAI architecture, a model can consume Kendra's authorised passages as retrieval context, but the application still needs grounding checks, source citations and appropriate prompt handling. When a policy answer seems stale, first inspect connector sync status and content access, not the inference model.

scenes.title: Amazon Kendra: improve retrieval quality
scenes.narration: This slide illustrates a second question: what makes a search result both relevant and permissible? A user asks where the support desk is, and the sample answer points to an IT Services Guide with an update date. The retrieval controls on the left include metadata filters, relevance tuning, freshness settings and feedback analytics. A department filter can narrow a result set, but it should complement enforced document access rather than act as the only security boundary. Relevance tuning can boost titles, keywords or selected fields so authoritative results rank higher. Freshness checks help identify whether a document has been superseded by a newer policy. Feedback and query analytics reveal searches with weak results or unhelpful ranking. Consider the full loop: filter to authorised content, rank by useful signals, retain the original source and update time, and measure user outcomes. Better search quality is not simply returning more documents; it is delivering the right evidence to the right person, with enough provenance to trust it.
